name: Purple Team Home Lab — Detection Coverage (v2 + v3)
description: Detection coverage for the Purple Team Home Lab (MARVEL.LOCAL AD), v2 (Sysmon + Splunk) and v3 (plus Zeek/Suricata NDR and Wazuh EDR). 15 techniques across 23 entries including tactic parents. Score 100 = exercised in the lab AND backed by shipped rule content in detections/. Score 75 = observed during the run with no rule committed for it (T1046, T1003.005, T1550.003). Score 50 = attempted but blocked or failed (v2/lab_issues.md). Scoring is about detection, not about whether the attack succeeded. Repo: github.com/slim92code/purple-team-lab

Detected — kerbrute userenum. Security EC4768 with result code 0x6 (KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN) in a burst from one source. The rule requires both a high count and a high distinct-name count, so a single mistyped service account does not trip it. Detection Card #1.

techniques.comment: Password spraying detected. See sub-technique T1110.003.

Detected — kerbrute password spray. Security EC4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failure) across many accounts from one source; the shipped rule correlates on the source address, not per-account counts. EC4625 only appears if kerbrute falls back to NTLM. The v2 spray recovered fcastle and triggered NO lockout, which is the point — one attempt per account per window stays under the threshold. EC4740 appears only after the Segment 10 FGPP fix, as the re-proof. v3 sprays onto pparker, a standard user. Detection Card #2.

techniques.comment: Kerberoasting detected. See sub-technique T1558.003.

Detected (v2 as RC4, v3 as AES) - Kerberoasting of the SQLService SPN via GetUserSPNs. The v2 roast came back RC4 (0x17) and the canonical rule caught it. The v3 roast came back AES-256 (0x12) and that same rule never fired: GetUserSPNs requested no etype and the KDC issued the strongest shared one (1,649 tickets over 30 days, all 0x12, zero 0x17). RC4 is not blocked on this domain - the Pass-the-Ticket step obtained an 0x17 TGT - the roast simply never asked for it. Shipped coverage for the AES case is the etype-agnostic companion (Sigma rule 10 / Purple - Kerberoasting User-SPN Ticket), which ships unscheduled pending a per-environment SPN allowlist. Detection Card #4.
Credential dumping — multiple sub-techniques exercised. See sub-techniques.

Detected (v3) — LSASS handle with a dump-capable GrantedAccess mask. SharpKatz ran in memory inside a process named notepad.exe and read lsass.exe at 0x1F3FFF. The mask list and the benign-reader exclusions are measured, not guessed: against 935 real reads sampled from the host, an earlier draft would have alerted 90 times with 89 of them benign. Telemetry was on one of three hosts during the v3 run; the Sysmon config gap was closed 25 Oct 2026 and the Wazuh ingestion gap 29 Oct 2026, so all three hosts now carry it - see config/README.md.

techniques.comment: Detected — SAM and SECURITY hives saved with reg.exe save through a Sliver shell (HKLM\SYSTEM was denied). impacket-secretsdump against the DC was blocked at port 445 and the local attempt failed with no SYSTEM hive, so it never recovered hashes. Defender flagged the reg save in real time (EC1116/1117); the shipped SIEM detection is the reg-save EC4688 rule, Detection Card #6.

techniques.comment: Detected — cached domain credentials (SECURITY hive). Detection Card #6. [NOT SHIPPED AS A RULE: exercised and recorded during the run, but no rule for it exists in detections/. Scored 75 so the map does not show it as rule coverage.]

GAP — DCSync attempt via SharpKatz FAILED. AMSI blocked Mimikatz; SharpKatz hit RPC error 1825 (Kerberos auth failure at DRS bind transport layer). Attempt telemetry captured by Sysmon EC1 but no successful replication. Blue-team win. See lab_issues.md.

techniques.comment: Remote services used for the east-west pivot. See sub-technique T1021.006.

Detected (v3) — WinRM pivot, SPIDERMAN to THEPUNISHER on TCP 5985 with the stolen ticket. Caught on the network layer: Zeek conn.log shows a workstation-to-workstation 5985 pair, which has no legitimate reason in an estate with no jump host. The Suricata REQUEST_AUTH_UNRECOGNIZED anomaly corroborates the timing but is not a WinRM signature and also fires on legitimate WinRM.
